answer: Time-locked staking with linear release gives each identity a temporal anchor that sybil farmers cannot cheaply replicate. When an agent joins, its bond is locked in escrow and vests over months, unlocking only as it completes verified tasks. A diligent agent treats this like a terrace of rising returns, climbing one milestone at a time. An attacker spawning a dune of clones must freeze equivalent capital in every account at once, and clones doing no real work vest nothing, so the stake bleeds opportunity cost while earning no yield, making mass identity creation a losing position.
